source: Federico Romagnoli, Gabriella Ferri: Da Roma alle Ande (OndaRock, 2014)
what_it_supports: Whole-record Roman/Neapolitan repertoire; Rosamunda polka, La pansé accelerando, La Luna layered voices and Beethoven motif; breakthrough, expressive intensity and moods.

source: RCA Italiana PSL 10534, original pressing credits (Recordsale)
what_it_supports: Original 1972 10-track album; Roberto Formentini producer; Guido and Maurizio De Angelis arrangers; Maurizio De Angelis guitar; original phonogram titles.

source: RCA/BMG 2002 reissue original notes (45cat)
what_it_supports: Original 1972 10 tracks, guitar and original producer confirmation, recording/re-recording engineer Sergio Patucchi (not a producer).

source: RCA Italiana LP genre/style transcription (musicbase)
what_it_supports: Original LP genre Pop / Folk / Chanson / Vocal; only first three treated as genres.

source: Maria Teresa Ferri interview, Patria Indipendente (2018)
what_it_supports: Rosamunda performance helped establish Ferri as a national star and connects to her folk heritage.

source: OndaRock album bibliography and chronology (1966–2000)
what_it_supports: Confirms this 1972 album distinct from 1971 Neapolitan LP and 1973 Sempre.

source: Federico Romagnoli, OndaRock monograph, Sempre section
what_it_supports: Album styles and sound: piano and synth on Io cerco la Titina, violin/polka on A casciaforte, guitar/keyboard on Cara madre mia, choir on Se ci vuoi pensar, nostalgic title ballad and waltz/march turns.

source: RCA Italiana DPSL 10588 original pressing notes (musicbase)
what_it_supports: Folk and chanson whole-record style, Roberto Formentini producer, musical arrangement division: Oddi, De Angelis, Bocci, Pisano; engineer Patucchi.

source: MusicBrainz, Sempre release credits and tracklist
what_it_supports: Ten tracks, lead vocals, orchestrated title single, track-level arrangers and Roberto Formentini credited as producer.

source: Sony BMG / Apple Music original 1973 album
what_it_supports: Album title and 1973 album with ten tracks; Pop category for the original programme.

source: OndaRock: 1973 TV and album reception and significance
what_it_supports: Sempre single became end theme to Dove sta Zazà TV show and the album career defining; theatrical transformation of folk music.

source: Federico Romagnoli, OndaRock monograph, Remedios section
what_it_supports: First half Latin American traditional repertoire, second half Roman; harmonica, orchestra, bass, mariachi brass, guitar, piano, percussion, strings, keyboards; intimate and uproarious moods.

source: Federico Romagnoli, OndaRock Pietra Miliare: Remedios
what_it_supports: Independent landmark assessment and distinctive two-sided album concept; folk/pop styles.

source: RCA Italiana TPL1 1046 original pressing (Potente Records)
what_it_supports: 11 original titles; original LP styles Latin, Pop, Folk, Tango, Ballad, Bolero; 1974 release.

source: 1974 RCA sleeve text transcribed by original-label collector (Mamma Lena)
what_it_supports: Original note Realizzazione di Cesare De Natale, arrangements Guido and Maurizio De Angelis, engineer Franco Finetti; not explicit Producer label.

source: 1974 RCA LP credit transcription (Vinileria)
what_it_supports: Credits Cesare De Natale as Technician/Realization and De Angelis as arrangers; no credited producer found.

source: Original Italian sound-recording credits reproduced by Sony/Qobuz
what_it_supports: Cesare De Natale listed only as Project Coordinator on 1974 songs, not a Producer; reason for empty producers column.

source: MusicBrainz, Remedios track metadata
what_it_supports: Tracklist: La paloma, Grazie alla vita, Cielito lindo, Remedios, La malagueña, La cucaracha, and five Roman songs; songs are covers not musical influences.

source: Giorgio Mancinelli, LaRecherche, Remedios retrospective
what_it_supports: Original 1974 Latin American and Roman programme, Spanish-language title composition and De Angelis arrangements.

source: Italian national library copyright bulletin, Remedios filing (1975)
what_it_supports: Contemporary bibliographic evidence for original sides, De Angelis arrangements and De Natale realization, distinct from production.

source: 900 Letterario: Remedios review
what_it_supports: Emphasis on Roman social narratives, Mexican and Spanish repertoire, emotional contrast in vocals, title track.

source: Federico Romagnoli, OndaRock monograph, Mazzabubù section
what_it_supports: Standard-based repertoire, departure of De Angelis, piano Moonlight Serenade interpolation in Vecchia Roma, shouted close to Malafemmena, limited songwriting, less experimentation.

source: RCA Italiana TPL1-1162 original LP credits (musicbase)
what_it_supports: 11-track 1975 studio LP; Cesare De Natale explicitly credited Producer, Gianni Oddi as director, Franco Finetti engineer; styles Ballad/Folk/Tango/Bolero.

source: Rai Teche: 50 years of the Mazzabubù TV show
what_it_supports: Rai television programme was separate from album, songs from mid-century Roman/Neapolitan and imported rhythms; distinct 1975 TV orchestral direction, NOT used for LP instruments.

source: La Stampa 30 October 1975 contemporary LP review (Totò archive)
what_it_supports: Original 1975 LP 11 songs; covers of Carosone, Buscaglione, Celentano, Totò, Roman/Neapolitan repertoire; period setting.

source: Hit Parade Italia historical 1976 original LP chart
what_it_supports: 1975 RCA album, original 11-title programme; chart appears in 1976 (not album release date), confirming independent record identity.

what_it_supports: Original Sony digital edition 1975 Pop; listed as 11 tracks unlike some later 12-track stream editions.

what_it_supports: Digital 12-track version adds Mazza Bubù as last title; do not treat this extra as part of original 11-track LP.

source: Original 1975 song credits reproduced by Qobuz
what_it_supports: The 1975 Mazzabubù tracks have Gianni Oddi and Flavio Bocci as arrangers; Cesare De Natale listed Project Coordinator; original LP credits clarify producer independently.

source: Musicbase Discogs-derived original LP style: Mazzabubù
what_it_supports: Folk/Ballad/Tango/Bolero with Pop/Latin cataloguing, not a uniformly rock album.
